videos.t: Neural networks to GPT, from first principles
videos.w: The full path from one neuron to a working GPT, with intuition first and code second.
videos.su: Three short 3Blue1Brown chapters give the picture of a network, gradient descent and backprop. Karpathy then builds backprop by hand (micrograd), a character-level language model (makemore), and a GPT, after 3Blue1Brown explains transformers and attention. It ends with the tokenizer, the part of an LLM most people skip.
videos.tk: You can write and train a small GPT yourself and explain every line.
videos.pr: Python and high-school calculus. No ML background needed.

videos.t: Making software fast
videos.w: Performance as a craft: measure honestly, respect the hardware, keep the code simple.
videos.su: Emery Berger on why most performance measurements are wrong, and Gil Tene on latency. Then the hardware view: Carruth on data structures, Mike Acton on data-oriented design, a cache-friendly hash table, and what the compiler does for you. Casey Muratori's philosophies of optimization and Netflix serving 800 Gb/s from one box close it out.
videos.tk: You know where time goes in a modern CPU and how to measure it without fooling yourself.
videos.pr: Some C, C++ or Rust helps.

videos.t: The history of computing, told by the people who built it
videos.w: From mechanical fire-control computers to Netscape, mostly in the builders' own words.
videos.su: James Burke traces computing back to its roots, then Navy training films explain mechanical computers and the Apollo Guidance Computer flies to the Moon. Silicon Valley's secret military history, Engelbart's 1968 demo and Sketchpad set up the modern era. Bell Labs explains UNIX, and Ken Thompson tells the story to Brian Kernighan. Alan Kay, the BBC's Micro Men, the Netscape documentary and Bret Victor finish it.
videos.tk: Where today's ideas came from, and which good ones we forgot.

videos.su: Writer and artist James Bridle shows how strange and disturbing children's videos on YouTube, from surprise eggs to algorithmic mashups, are produced for ad revenue. He argues they reveal problems in a data-driven internet.

m.x: This TED talk sums up why I'll never allow my child to go on YouTube.
m.st: ChuChu TV is responsible for widely-viewed toddler content on YouTube

videos.t: CppCon 2016: Chandler Carruth “High Performance Code 201: Hybrid Data Structures"
videos.w: Cited as the source for criticism of std::deque and move-constructor pitfalls, and as motivation to write custom data structures.
videos.su: Chandler Carruth's CppCon 2016 talk on designing hybrid data structures for performance. He covers cache locality, working-set size and allocation overhead, and why standard C++ containers fall short.

m.x: I suggest watching this talk
m.st: EASTL: An Alternative C++ Standard Library

videos.t: Steve Yegge, "What Would You Do With Your Own Google?" - OSCON Data 2011
videos.w: Cited for its critique of talent wasted on social media and for the data-mining-for-biology argument, plus the around-14-minute quitting moment.
videos.su: Steve Yegge's OSCON Data 2011 talk imagines what you could do with Google-scale storage and compute a decade later. He argues smart people should work on hard problems such as biology rather than cat pictures, and the talk ends with a moment many took as him quitting Google.

m.x: this is an excellent talk about preparing to solve hard problems in bio.
m.st: BioCurious, a hackerspace for bio now open to public

videos.t: The Problem with America’s Lab Mice and Why it Should Matter to You
videos.w: HN links it when discussing mouse-study reliability and reproducibility.
videos.su: A JRE clip in which Bret Weinstein explains his concern that most American lab mice descend from a single lab lineage. He argues this undermines how well mouse research translates to humans.

m.x: Here's the actual segment (18 mins)
m.st: Cracking down on research fraud

videos.su: A surreal multimedia TEDxSarasota performance by Magic Leap founder Rony Abovitz, held on 12/12/12, mixing performance art with talk about imagination and creativity.

m.x: This is a good video on it
